title: Marlins’ Sandy Alcantara Starter-Reliever Pitching Strategy Trends in MLB Playoffs
description: The Miami Marlins aren’t playing in the 2026 MLB playoffs. After a promising start to the season, they eventually settled into a middle-of-the-pack role that saw them head home after the final day of the regular season. Despite that, the Marlins are currently having a fascinating impact on the proceedings in the postseason, with both […] The post Marlins’ Sandy Alcantara Starter-Reliever Pitching Strategy Trends in MLB Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Miami Marlins aren't playing in the 2026 MLB playoffs. After a promising start to the season, they eventually settled into a middle-of-the-pack role that saw them head home after the final day of the regular season.

Despite that, the Marlins are currently having a fascinating impact on the proceedings in the postseason, with both the Cleveland Guardians and San Diego Padres in particular employing a strategy Miami used late in the season to great effect with ace Sandy Alcantara.

There are often fancy pitching strategies used in the playoffs that are rarely used in the regular season, but in this case, the Marlins provided a sneak peak at the end of the 2026 campaign.

The Marlins did something quite unusual with their ace righty Sandy Alcantara down the stretch of the season: They brought him out of the bullpen for a pair of saves.

He didn't miss any turns through the starting rotation, either. These were like bonus outings.

The Marlins actually did it once with 6-foot-8 right-handed starter Eury Perez, as well.

The Marlins appeared to be testing whether a starting pitcher could throw his so-called "bullpen day" in an actual MLB game.

Starting pitchers in professional baseball generally have one hefty bullpen workout in between starts. It's a chance to refine mechanics and stay sharp while also keeping the arm active rather than just not throwing at all for four or five days.

That's been the approach for decades as teams have relied more and more on relief pitching in recent years while trying to avoid injuries to their key starting pitchers.

The only time starting pitchers ever came out of the bullpen, at least the top-notch starters, was to be a hero in the playoffs. There's also the opener-into-bulk pitching approach that isn't what this is.

Nope, the Marlins were bringing in their starters on their assigned bullpen day, using the pitches they were going to throw anyway during game action instead of out of sight.

It's now been used multiple times in the MLB playoffs.

The Padres did it first, earlier this week using Michael King out of the bullpen on what would've been his usual work on the side day and getting six outs from him with regular closer Mason Miller on the paternity list. King would've been available to pitch his usual start day if the Padres hadn't been eliminated the next day.

The Guardians then did it on Thursday night with Gavin Williams. He's still slated to start ALDS Game 5 on Saturday, but Thursday was his bullpen day and he threw 18 pitches to get three outs in the ninth inning to force the decisive fifth game.

It's not yet clear if this is a sustainable long-term strategy, but teams definitely are thinking about those bullpen days as usable if needed.

Obviously, pitches in a high-intensity playoff game are more stressful than those thrown in a quiet bullpen session, so the effects of this will still need to be watched.

But clearly, the Marlins were onto something. Other teams are trying it, too.

title: Daniel Suárez Signs Contract Extension to Remain With Spire Motorsports Through 2027
description: Suárez Secures His Future With Spire Daniel Suárez will continue driving for Spire Motorsports after signing a contract extension that keeps him with the organization through the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series season. The agreement provides stability for Suárez and the No. 7 Chevrolet team as they look to build on their progress together. Suárez joined…
fullText:
Daniel Suárez will continue driving for Spire Motorsports after signing a contract extension that keeps him with the organization through the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series season. The agreement provides stability for Suárez and the No. 7 Chevrolet team as they look to build on their progress together.

Suárez joined Spire ahead of the 2026 season after spending five years with Trackhouse Racing. The move gave him a fresh opportunity with an organization continuing to grow its presence in NASCAR's top series.

Now, with his future secured through 2027, Suárez can focus on competing for victories and helping Spire establish itself as a consistent contender.

Suárez has given Spire plenty of reasons to believe the partnership can succeed. One of the biggest highlights of the 2026 campaign came when he won the Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte Motor Speedway.

The victory was a major achievement for Suárez, who entered the season looking to get back into Victory Lane after a challenging final year at Trackhouse. Winning one of NASCAR's most prestigious races also demonstrated the potential of the No. 7 team.

Suárez has worked closely with crew chief Ryan Sparks to improve the team's performance and build stronger communication throughout race weekends. Their developing relationship has been an important part of the group's progress.

The extension gives the driver and crew chief additional time to continue developing their program without uncertainty surrounding Suárez's future.

Keeping Suárez through 2027 is another important step for Spire Motorsports as it continues strengthening its Cup Series operation.

The organization fields three full-time Cup Series teams, with Suárez joined by Michael McDowell and Carson Hocevar. Maintaining stability across its lineup can help Spire continue developing its equipment, sharing information and improving its overall competitiveness.

Suárez also brings valuable experience to the organization, having won multiple Cup Series races and competed at NASCAR's highest level for several seasons.

With his contract extended through 2027, Suárez can turn his attention toward the remainder of the season and the challenges ahead.

The goal now is to build on the success of 2026, contend for more victories and continue helping Spire Motorsports take the next step. The extension gives both sides a chance to keep building something special together.

title: Blades Brown posts back-to-back eagles, shoots 61, on the brink of PGA Tour card
description: Blades Brown was 1 under through eight holes in his second round at the Korn Ferry Tour Championship. Then he turned on the jets.
fullText:
Blades Brown was 1 under through eight holes in his second round at the Korn Ferry Tour Championship. Then he turned on the jets.

After making back-to-back eagles at Nos. 9 and 10, Brown had three straight pars but then closed with five straight birdies. Add it up and after being 1 under through 8, he went 9 under over his last 10 holes to shoot 10-under 61 and take the outright lead in the circuit's season finale.

Brown walked off the course with the clubhouse lead at 13 under, one ahead of Austin Hitt, who also went low Friday with a 62.

The top 20 finishers in the season-long points race earn 2027 PGA Tour cards and 13 golfers had already reached that mark. Brown started the KFT Championship as the highest in the points without having yet secured a card.

Through 36 holes, he's vaulted to fourth. Nothing is final yet, but should he avoid disaster, Brown, at 19 years, 4 months and 22 days old, would become the youngest golfer to earn PGA Tour status via the KFT. Jason Day holds the mark at 19 years, 11 months and 23 days.

Brown made the surprising decision to turn pro at age 17 at the end of 2024.

"I know my route to the PGA Tour is a very uncommon route," Brown said. "It's mainly because of my parents. They've been my biggest supporters. They've sacrificed so much, especially my dad. He's been – I think he's missed about two events in my entire life, and he believed in me whenever I didn't believe in myself."

At the CJ Cup Byron Nelson earlier this year, a tie for 14th clinched Special Temporary Membership on the PGA Tour. He proceeded to spend the rest of his 2026 chasing points on the KFT and it's about to pay off.

This article originally appeared on Golfweek: Blades Brown posts back-to-back eagles, shoots 61, on the brink of PGA Tour card

title: Eagles Cut Ties With Former Bears Starting Quarterback
description: The Philadelphia Eagles have cut ties with former Chicago Bears quarterback Andy Dalton after poor showing against Chicago. The post Eagles Cut Ties With Former Bears Starting Quarterback appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles are making a quarterback change, cutting ties with former Chicago Bears QB Andy Dalton prior to their Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

"The #Eagles are releasing QB Andy Dalton, sources say," NFL insider Mike Garafolo posted on X. "Tanner McKee and Cole Payton will be the backups to Jalen Hurts moving forward."

The Eagles actually traded for Dalton this past offseason, sending a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Carolina Panthers to acquire the veteran quarterback.

He had a 3-3 record as a starter for the Bears from 2021-2022.

Andy Dalton came in after Jalen Hurts took a massive hit from Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson during the Week 3 battle, and rookie safety Dillon Thieneman intercepted his only pass.

After the game, Dalton commented on his mistake, saying, "I thought they said something for an injury timeout. So I thought that I was going to be going in just at least for one play because I didn't know exactly what it was. …We get down there, I can't put ourselves in a bad position like that. I mean, costly turnover at a tough time, man. That's points on the board."

"[The Bears] schemed it up pretty good." I obviously didn't see the safety in the middle, and he just read my eyes. My eyes were over there, and he just made the play. Again, I can't put our team in that situation. Costly decision."

Well, he's no longer on the Eagles. However, Mike Garafolo didn't rule out Dalton coming back on the practice squad. "This doesn't close the door on Andy Dalton's tenure with the #Eagles," Garafolo added. "They have a lot of injuries and needed his spot. Could still return, even via a practice-squad spot, a source informed says."

Things are trending in the right direction for Bears quarterback Caleb Williams.

At least, according to Ben Johnson.

"We got him progressively increasing the amount of running that's going on, and of course the throwing aspect of it is a big part of his position as well. Our guys have a good plan in place and we're just going step by step with that right now."

title: Charlotte Motor Speedway to host Kyle Busch celebration of life
description: NASCAR legend Kyle Busch will be honored with a celebration of life Friday night at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
fullText:
NASCAR fans, friends, and family gathered at Charlotte Motor Speedway to honor the life of legendary driver, philanthropist, and family man Kyle Busch. Busch died in late May from severe pneumonia that turned into sepsis.

The track tribute served as the second honor dedicated to Busch. Earlier in the day, the NASCAR Hall of Fame opened a new exhibit titled "Kyle Busch: Honoring a Legacy" to commemorate his 25-year racing career.

Busch's family unveiled the No. 18 car from his first NASCAR Cup Series championship as part of the display.

His wife, Samantha Busch, shared that while many cars could have been selected for the exhibit, the championship vehicle represents far more than just a single victory.

Throughout his career, Busch became the winningest overall driver in NASCAR history, recording 234 victories across NASCAR's three main series: the Cup Series, the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series and the Craftsman Truck Series.

Race enthusiasts displayed Kyle Busch flags on tents and campers around the Concord campground prior to entering the speedway.

Greg McInnis, a Kyle Busch fan at the venue, highlighted the importance of remembering the driver alongside fellow fans.

"Being able to wrap that with the NASCAR community here at home in Charlotte is going to do wonders for the sport," McInnis said. "Not only for just the sport but for everybody included in NASCAR."

The 8 p.m. celebration of life ceremony is taking place on the track's infield after the EcoSave 200 NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series race.

Admission and parking were offered free to fans attending the tribute, where Busch's loved ones and friends were scheduled to speak.

title: Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Gets Bad News Ahead of Jets Game
description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel received some bad news ahead of the team's Week 5 matchup against the New York Jets. The post Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Gets Bad News Ahead of Jets Game appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns are giving Dillon Gabriel more time before bringing him back to the active roster.

The second-year quarterback was ruled out Friday for Cleveland's Week 5 matchup against the New York Jets. Gabriel returned to practice Wednesday following a stint on injured reserve with a back injury, but he will not be activated to the 53-man roster for Sunday's game.

The decision gives Gabriel another week to get comfortable on the field and delays a roster squeeze at quarterback. Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders and rookie Taylen Green already occupy spots on the active roster.

Head coach Todd Monken indicated earlier in the week that Cleveland felt little urgency to activate Gabriel. The Browns opened his return window this week, allowing him to practice while remaining on injured reserve.

"Get him out there, practice, see where he's at with his back, and get the reps that we can get," Monken said during his October 7 news conference.

Monken said much of that work would come through individual drills and scout-team reps. For Gabriel, the immediate opportunity is to get back into a routine after missing the first four games.

The Browns announced Gabriel's eligibility to return to practice Tuesday. His 21-day window gives Cleveland time to assess his progress before deciding whether to activate him. If he is not activated before that window expires, he will remain on injured reserve for the rest of the season.

Gabriel landed on IR after injuring his back during the preseason finale against the New England Patriots. That outing had given him something to build on: he completed 12 of 15 passes for 186 yards and three touchdowns.

Gabriel started six games as a rookie in 2025, completing 59.5% of his passes for 937 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. His next role will depend on both his recovery and how Cleveland arranges the depth behind Watson. Gabriel is not expected to leapfrog Sanders for the No. 2 spot, but the Browns have revealed little about their quarterback depth and the decision to keep four passers on the roster.

Gabriel's return to practice has put the quarterback numbers back in focus. Activating Gabriel while retaining the other three would mean using four of the team's 53 roster spots on quarterbacks. Cleveland would have to weigh that depth against needs elsewhere.

Those needs are immediate on the defensive line. Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. have been ruled out against the Jets, and Kalia Davis — who was on IR like Gabriel — also will not return this week.

Monken declined Wednesday to settle the four-quarterback question, pointing to the time remaining in Gabriel's practice window.

"The three-week window to kind of see where we're at. So that's kind of where we're at. Get him out there, practice, see where he's at with his back, and get the reps that we can get," Monken said. "I look forward to seeing him back out there."

With Cleveland entering Sunday at 3-1 and seeking a fourth consecutive win, Sanders remains next in line behind Watson. Gabriel can continue practicing while the Browns evaluate when to bring him back and where he fits.

title: 99-Year-Old NASCAR Fan Finally Gets Her Dream Ride at Michigan Speedway
description: Shirley Hipple has followed NASCAR for nearly 70 years. As her 100th birthday approaches, the Michigan superfan finally got to experience the thrill of riding in a stock car at Michigan International Speedway.
fullText:
For nearly 70 years, Shirley Hipple experienced NASCAR the same way millions of fans do: from the comfort of her living room, watching the cars race around the track on television.

But at 99 years old, with her 100th birthday approaching, Hipple finally got to experience something she'd spent decades watching from afar.

She climbed into a stock car at Michigan International Speedway and went for a ride.

The experience, arranged through a senior living community's adventure program, gave the longtime NASCAR fan a chance to hear the engines, feel the speed and see the track from a perspective she had only imagined.

And after seven decades of following the sport, it was quite a way to celebrate a milestone birthday.

Hipple's love for racing dates back to the 1950s, when she took her young children to dirt tracks near Groesbeck Highway and Eight Mile Road in Detroit.

What began as family outings developed into a lifelong passion. She followed NASCAR through generations of drivers, championship battles and changes to the sport, rarely missing a race on television.

Her favorite driver became seven-time Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, whose jacket she proudly wore as part of her racing collection.

According to Kinship Company, Hipple even turned her room at Waltonwood Carriage Park in Canton, Michigan, into a tribute to the sport she loved.

But there was one experience she had never checked off her list: actually riding in a stock car.

Through Waltonwood's Adventure program, which helps residents fulfill longtime wishes, Hipple traveled to Michigan International Speedway for a NASCAR ride-along.

Dressed in racing gear and secured inside the car, she experienced the speed and banking of the two-mile oval firsthand.

For someone who had spent nearly 70 years watching NASCAR on television, it was an entirely different way to appreciate the sport.

The ride wasn't the only highlight of Hipple's visit.

She also received a behind-the-scenes tour of pit road, giving her an up-close look at a part of NASCAR that fans typically experience only through television coverage.

The trip was especially meaningful because it connected Hipple's earliest memories of racing in Detroit with one of Michigan's most recognizable motorsports venues.

Sara Bailey, vice president of sales for Waltonwood, said the experience reflected the purpose of the community's Adventure program.

"At Waltonwood, we believe that passions don't fade with age," Bailey said. "Seeing Shirley's lifelong dream come true is what our Adventure program is all about."

Hipple's story is a reminder of something NASCAR fans understand particularly well: A connection to racing can last a lifetime.

Drivers retire, teams change and the cars evolve, but the excitement that first draws someone to the sport can remain remarkably familiar.

For Hipple, that excitement began at local dirt tracks in the 1950s and eventually carried her all the way to Michigan International Speedway.

Now, as she approaches her 100th birthday, she has a new racing memory to add to a collection nearly seven decades in the making.

And this time, she didn't have to watch it on television.

title: Chiefs’ Offense Could Get Massive $35M Boost With Potential Trade Target
description: The Chiefs' offense could benefit from a trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., but acquiring the Cardinals receiver would come with some complications.
fullText:
Patrick Mahomes probably isn't losing much sleep over the Chiefs' 4-0 start. Kansas City keeps winning, and that's generally enough to keep everyone happy. But take a closer look at the Chiefs' offense, specifically the receiving corps, and it's fair to wonder how long they can keep getting away with it.

Tyquan Thornton hurt his ankle against Las Vegas. Rashee Rice has been dealing with a hamstring injury. The Chiefs' offense scored 30 points against the Raiders anyway, thanks in large part to Kenneth Walker III running for 177 yards. Nice when that happens. Not something you want to depend on every week, though.

ESPN's Dan Graziano recently brought up Marvin Harrison Jr. as a possible trade target for the Chiefs' offense if Arizona decides to entertain offers.

Harrison? Two years after the Cardinals took him fourth overall?

It sounds a little ridiculous until you look at his numbers.

He caught 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie in 2024. Nothing wrong with that, although expectations were considerably higher for someone drafted ahead of so many other talented receivers.

His second season was less encouraging. Harrison finished with 41 catches for 608 yards in 12 games.

And this year? Five receptions for 85 yards through four games.

Those are the kinds of numbers that get people talking, especially when the player involved entered the league with Harrison's reputation.

The Chiefs' offense could offer him something Arizona hasn't consistently provided: a chance to work with an established quarterback in a system that's been successful for years.

But that doesn't mean Kansas City should automatically jump at the opportunity. Giving Harrison Jr. the opportunity to work alongside Mahomes could really bolster the Chiefs' offense.

Arizona spent the fourth overall pick on Harrison in 2024. Giving up on that investment after two seasons would be quite a decision, even if the production hasn't matched expectations.

The Cardinals would presumably want substantial compensation, and Kansas City would have to decide how much it's willing to surrender for a receiver who hasn't established himself as a consistent difference maker.

There's also the question of whether Harrison wants to leave.

"Truthfully, I pay it no mind," he said Thursday when asked about the rumors.

That doesn't sound like someone campaigning for a trade.

Harrison recently hired agents Todd France and Tory Dandy, but there's no reason to assume that decision means he's preparing to force his way out of Arizona.

The financial side is interesting, too.

Harrison signed a four-year rookie contract worth approximately $35.4 million. That's the total value of his original deal, not what another team would have to pay Arizona to acquire him.

For the Chiefs' offense, the appeal would be getting a young receiver without immediately taking on the salary of an established veteran star.

The draft picks are where things could get expensive.

Here's the question Kansas City needs to answer: How much better would Harrison actually make this team in 2026?

The Chiefs' offense has already found ways to win despite injuries. Mahomes has worked with changing receiver groups before, and Andy Reid isn't suddenly going to forget how to call plays because a couple of wideouts are unavailable.

Harrison would have to learn a new offense in the middle of the season. He'd also need time to develop chemistry with Mahomes.

That's not necessarily an easy transition, regardless of talent.

On the other hand, the Chiefs have a chance to acquire a receiver who was considered one of the best prospects in the 2024 draft. He's only 24, and his struggles in Arizona don't erase the ability that made him such a highly regarded player.

There's a difference between a bad player and a talented player stuck in a bad situation. Harrison might simply need a different environment. The Chiefs' offense doesn't need him to become the next Tyreek Hill. It needs another reliable option who can make defenses think twice about loading up against Kansas City's other weapons.

If Arizona is willing to discuss a reasonable deal, Veach should listen. If the Cardinals demand multiple premium picks, that's another story.

The Chiefs are now 4-0. It has no reason to panic, and an undefeated team shouldn't start treating every injury like a roster emergency.

But Kansas City also knows how quickly things can change over a long NFL season. Harrison is an intriguing possibility for the Chiefs' offense, not a necessity. The distinction is important, especially with November 10 getting closer.

Sometimes the best trade deadline decision is recognizing when the price is too high.

And sometimes a phone call lands you a player who wasn't supposed to be available in the first place.

title: Michael King Gets Honest About Potential Future With The Padres
description: Padres right-handed starter Michael King, after the Padres’ elimination from the postseason by the Milwaukee Brewers, expressed optimism about a potential return to San Diego this winter. King is 31 years old and posted a 3.21 ERA this year in San Diego, with 159 strikeouts in 185 innings and a 1.18 WHIP.King told Jeff Sanders, […] The post Michael King Gets Honest About Potential Future With The Padres appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Padres right-handed starter Michael King, after the Padres' elimination from the postseason by the Milwaukee Brewers, expressed optimism about a potential return to San Diego this winter. King is 31 years old and posted a 3.21 ERA this year in San Diego, with 159 strikeouts in 185 innings and a 1.18 WHIP.

King told Jeff Sanders, a reporter for the San Diego Tribune, that his "option is a future decision," but that he's been upfront all along about what San Diego has meant to him: "This is where I started a family," King told Sanders. King went on to tell Sanders that being on the West Coast "has felt like a second home to him" and added, "so it's been awesome. And yeah, I would hope it continues," King told Sanders. King re-signed with the Padres last offseason on a three-year $75 million contract that included player opt-outs for the first two seasons (2027, 2028).

While King's future in San Diego is currently up in the air, he had a solid 2026 campaign with the Padres and pitched very well in the postseason, compiling a 0.64 ERA in three games. King pitched seven shutout innings against the Cubs in game one of the Wild Card, and pitched five innings of one-run ball in game two against the Milwaukee Brewers, which the Padres would go on to lose dramatically due to a walk-off two-run base hit in the bottom of the ninth from Jackson Chourio off Padres electric closer Mason Miller.

King then threw 40 pitches in two innings out of the bullpen in game three to secure a Padres 4-3 win after starting just two days prior, because closer Mason Miller was placed on the paternity list and was therefore not available to pitch. King had a solid market as a starter last offseason, and he probably will again this offseason if he opts out of his three-year deal with the Padres. The Yankees traded King to the Padres in the 2023-24 offseason, and the Yankees acquired Juan Soto and Trent Grisham in return.

King was a durable pitcher for the Yankees back then, and he's been durable for the Padres over the past three years in San Diego. It will be interesting to see if the mutual relationship between the Padres and King continues. King supposedly loves San Diego, and the Padres love him, as shown by their financial commitment. But King has to decide if he wants to test the open market again this winter. The Padres are also under new ownership with Kwanza Jones and Jose E. Feliciano. Do the Padres still pursue King if he decides to opt out?

It's also important to remember that Major League Baseball and the players' union are facing a lockout this offseason, so how will that affect the free agency market and King's decision in the coming weeks?

title: Carrick’s wildcard move to play Bruno Fernandes in an unusual role will solve two major problems at United
description: Manchester United’s uninspiring transfer business over the summer has put head coach Michael Carrick in a difficult situation.In their bid to overhaul United’s midfield, Jason Wilcox and company o...
fullText:
Manchester United's uninspiring transfer business over the summer has put head coach Michael Carrick in a difficult situation.

In their bid to overhaul United's midfield, Jason Wilcox and company overlooked other areas of the field. The decision not to bring in a left-back or a striker is starting to seem like a huge oversight.

Ahead of United's clash against Tottenham Hotspur, Carrick confirmed that Patrick Dorgu and Benjamin Sesko would be unavailable due to injury. A shin injury has kept Sesko in and out of the side since the second half of last season, forcing Carrick to rely on the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Joshua Zirkzee.

All three players have underwhelmed while leading United's attack for different reasons, and with Sesko still sidelined, it is time for Carrick to look for another solution.

In that regard, one player who has proven to be a jack of all trades and a master as well under several managers over the past six years could prove to be an answer to the persistent striker problem under Carrick.

After an impressive stint as a box-to-box midfielder under Ruben Amorim, Bruno Fernandes returned to his favoured number 10 position following Michael Carrick's arrival at the turn of the year.

After being positioned higher up the pitch, Fernandes also returned to his devastating best and finished the campaign with the Premier League assist record to his name.

A few United managers, including Ralf Rangnick and Erik ten Hag, have made the most of Fernandes' attacking prowess by pushing him even higher, as a false nine.

In the absence of a natural striker in the FA Cup final against Manchester City in 2024, Ten Hag trusted Fernandes to spearhead the attack as a false nine. The Portuguese delivered a stellar performance and registered a sublime no-look assist for Kobbie Mainoo's match-winning strike.

Without a doubt, Fernandes is currently one of the best passers in European football, but he is also a ferocious striker of the ball, boasting a variety of finishing options in his locker. He has more goals than assists under his belt at both United and former club Sporting CP.

The 32-year-old star has already shown how lethal he is in front of goal this season with a hat-trick against Ipswich Town.

The most commendable aspect of Fernandes' game is that, irrespective of his role, he never stops working tirelessly and consistently tries to lead the side's press.

Moreover, his ability to drop deep as a false nine would leave acres of space for the likes of Marcus Rashford and Mbeumo to exploit.

During previous managerial reigns, United's build-up suffered whenever Fernandes was asked to stay up front, with the Red Devils lacking midfielders capable of progressing the play from deep.

That is not the case anymore, as both Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are technically gifted midfielders, possessing dribbling ability and passing range to effectively find their teammates in the final third.

The decision to move Fernandes as a striker would also pave the way for Carlos Baleba to come into the starting line-up and form an exciting midfield trio.

Baleba is an excellent ball carrier and an even better ball winner, who would take both the intensity and physicality of the midfield up a notch.

The Portuguese maestro is a decisive player who has the game intelligence and positional awareness to be a dangerous presence anywhere in the final third. Now, United have a midfield that would not cry out for their captain to make things happen all the time, handing Carrick a brilliant opportunity to make the striker shortage at Old Trafford a blessing in disguise.

title: Brewers Receive Bold Prediction Ahead of NLCS Date With Dodgers
description: The Milwaukee Brewers secured their spot in the National League Championship Series with a 3-1 win over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 of the Division Series. Just like 2025, the Brewers have the first two games at […] The post Brewers Receive Bold Prediction Ahead of NLCS Date With Dodgers appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers secured their spot in the National League Championship Series with a 3-1 win over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 of the Division Series. Once again, they will face the Los Angeles Dodgers, who swept them in last year's NLCS. Just like 2025, the Brewers have the first two games at home by virtue of having the best record in Major League Baseball.

The Dodgers won the series easily last year, but the Brewers are looking for redemption. The Dodgers may be the favorites, but not everybody believes that they are going to win this series. In fact, Buster Olney of ESPN believes that the Brewers are going to be the ones walking away victorious instead.

"I think the Milwaukee Brewers are going to win because they're in a much better position with their pitching," Olney said on Friday.

Shoutout Buster. pic.twitter.com/LTsIi3sCw7

— ESPN Milwaukee (@ESPNMilwaukee) October 9, 2026

To be fair, the Brewers are starting this series at home. They beat the Padres in four games in the Division Series, which leaves Jacob Misiorowski in line to start Game 1 of the NLCS on Sunday night.

Unlike last year, Misiorowski has unlocked his full potential and been perhaps the best starting pitcher in Major League Baseball, so having him at home to open the series is a big advantage for Milwaukee.

That also means that they will likely have Logan Henderson on the mound for Game 2 of the series. The pitching staff is in a much better spot this year than it was at this time last year.

That isn't to say that facing the Dodgers is going to be an easy task for them. The Dodgers have still won back-to-back World Series titles, and will likely be considered the favorites to win by most.

But Olney clearly sees something he likes better about the Brewers in this series, and a lot of it could have to do with Misiorowski being fully seasoned. But it's also important to remember that the Brewers set a franchise record in regular season wins again, this time winning 103 games before ultimately knocking out the Padres. So, a case can be made that they are a more formidable opponent this time around.

It still won't be easy, but there could be something different about this year's Brewers team that gives them a better chance of taking down the Dodgers and reaching the World Series for the first time since 1982.

If the Dodgers stick with the order they used in the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves, that would line Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell up to pitch the first two games, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto for Game 3 back in Los Angeles, so the pitching matchups are going to be tough for Milwaukee.

But there is a lot to like about what the Brewers have to offer, so it should be a very entertaining series as the two teams fight it out to determine who will reach the World Series for the National League.

title: Jeff Hafley Fires Back After Bengals Player Reveals Malik Willis Habit
description: The Miami Dolphins are searching for their first victory of the 2026 NFL season as they prepare to host the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5. Head coach Jeff Hafley’s team has lost its first four games and needs a stronger offensive performance to turn its season around.Quarterback Malik Willis will be under pressure to improve […] The post Jeff Hafley Fires Back After Bengals Player Reveals Malik Willis Habit appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Miami Dolphins are searching for their first victory of the 2026 NFL season as they prepare to host the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5. Head coach Jeff Hafley's team has lost its first four games and needs a stronger offensive performance to turn its season around.

Quarterback Malik Willis will be under pressure to improve after struggling in Miami's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

The Dolphins managed only 85 passing yards from Willis in that game, while a lost fumble added to their offensive problems. Miami now faces a Cincinnati defense preparing to exploit any weaknesses it has identified.

The Bengals enter the matchup with a 2-2 record, while Miami is still looking for consistency with its young roster. Ahead of Sunday's meeting at Hard Rock Stadium, comments from a Cincinnati defensive back have prompted Hafley to address one particular aspect of Willis' throwing mechanics.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley responds to Bengals DB Jordan Battle's statement regarding a "tell" that QB Malik Willis has #PhinsUp pic.twitter.com/DUu5g8tXU7

— c. isaiah smalls ii (@stclaudeii) October 9, 2026

Miami Herald reporter C. Isaiah Smalls II reported that Hafley responded after Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle suggested that Willis has a habit that defenders could use to anticipate his passes.

Battle previously said, "He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball."

"He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read the break."

Battle also warned that Cincinnati must account for Willis' mobility.

He said the quarterback can extend plays and run quarterback draws on third-and-long situations, requiring defenders to remain alert even when the initial play breaks down.

Hafley, however, played down the significance of the alleged throwing tell.

The Dolphins coach said he has studied quarterbacks for more than 25 years and has seen similar movements throughout his career.

"I studied quarterbacks for over 25 years, and that is not uncommon," Hafley said Friday.

"A lot of quarterbacks pat the ball or take their hand off the ball. There are some I've studied that look up right before they throw the ball. I don't think there's anything revolutionary about that."

Hafley described the movement as a matter of timing and rhythm rather than an unusual tendency. He also welcomed Cincinnati's decision to discuss the matter publicly.

"It's a timing and rhythm thing with a lot of guys, and there's a lot of them that do that, but any opponent that wants to share our tendencies with us, we'll take any time," Hafley said.

Willis' performances give the discussion added significance.

Through four games, he has completed 56.3% of his passes for 712 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

He has also recorded 119 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on 19 attempts.

After the loss to Minnesota, Willis acknowledged that the team's results and execution were not good enough.

Sunday's matchup will test whether Miami can improve against a defense that believes it has identified a potential advantage.

While Willis prepares for Cincinnati's defensive approach, Miami is also relying on its young players to help establish a stronger foundation under Hafley.

The Dolphins' rookies have combined for 1,726 snaps through four games, the most in the NFL.

Their playing time has provided valuable experience as the team continues to develop despite its 0-4 record.

Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez credited Hafley's confidence and preparation with helping him play faster and work effectively with his teammates.

"Coach Hafley gives me a lot of confidence," Rodriguez said.

"I think the confidence that he has in me instills confidence, and I have so much respect and confidence in him."

Chris Bell also expressed belief in the team's progress, emphasizing the relationships developing within the locker room.

"We work so hard week in and week out, every week," Bell said.

"And I can feel this team coming together, and we are a brotherhood, and a family."

The Dolphins now have an opportunity to translate that development into their first win.

Hafley's response to Battle has made clear that Miami does not consider Willis' throwing motion an extraordinary concern, but the quarterback must still improve his execution against Cincinnati's defense.

title: Former Panthers QB Andy Dalton Gets Unfortunate NFL News With Eagles
description: The Eagles' Andy Dalton experiment appears to be over after just one pass. A look back at the former Panthers quarterback's career. The post Former Panthers QB Andy Dalton Gets Unfortunate NFL News With Eagles appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Former Carolina Panthers quarterback Andy Dalton is reportedly being released by the Philadelphia Eagles, bringing an abrupt end to his time with the defending NFC East champions.

Dalton, 38, was acquired from Carolina in March in exchange for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick. But after spending three seasons as Bryce Young's backup and occasional replacement, the veteran struggled to establish himself in Philadelphia.

His regular-season numbers with the Eagles tell the story: one game, one pass attempt, zero completions and one interception.

Dalton briefly replaced Jalen Hurts during Philadelphia's Week 3 matchup against the Chicago Bears while Hurts underwent a concussion evaluation. His lone pass was intercepted in the end zone by rookie safety Dillon Thieneman.

The Eagles subsequently moved Tanner McKee ahead of Dalton on the depth chart for their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.

The #Eagles are releasing QB Andy Dalton, sources say.

Tanner McKee and Cole Payton will be the backups to Jalen Hurts moving forward. pic.twitter.com/1t9mlxFRjq

— Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 9, 2026

The Eagles acquired Dalton hoping his extensive NFL experience would provide insurance behind Hurts.

Dalton entered the 2026 season with 15 years of NFL experience and 169 career starts, giving Philadelphia a proven veteran option in a quarterback room that also included McKee.

However, Dalton's performance in limited regular-season action did little to strengthen his case for the backup job.

After his interception against Chicago, NFL Network reported that McKee would replace Dalton as Philadelphia's No. 2 quarterback, leaving the former Panthers starter third on the depth chart.

The decision represented a quick reversal for a quarterback Philadelphia had traded for only months earlier.

Carolina, meanwhile, had already received its return in the deal. The Panthers acquired a 2027 seventh-round draft selection while moving on from a veteran who had spent three seasons behind Young.

Dalton joined the Panthers in 2023, serving primarily as a backup while making seven starts across three seasons.

In 13 total appearances with Carolina, Dalton completed 165 of 255 passes for 1,643 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

His record as a Panthers starter was 1-6, although his individual performances varied considerably.

Dalton's first start for Carolina came against the Seattle Seahawks in September 2023, when he threw for 361 yards and two touchdowns in a 37-27 defeat.

His most memorable Panthers performance came the following season.

After head coach Dave Canales benched Bryce Young in September 2024, Dalton stepped in against the Las Vegas Raiders and delivered Carolina's first victory of the season.

Dalton completed 26 of 37 attempts for 319 yards and three touchdowns without an interception in the Panthers' 36-22 win.

It was an encouraging performance for Carolina, which had struggled offensively during the opening weeks of the season.

But the momentum did not last. Dalton lost his next four starts in 2024, and Young eventually reclaimed the starting job.

Dalton made one additional start during the 2025 season, completing 16 of 24 passes for 175 yards and an interception in a loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Despite his brief stint in Philadelphia, Dalton has put together an extensive NFL career dating back to 2011.

The Cincinnati Bengals selected Dalton in the second round of the 2011 NFL Draft, and he spent nine seasons as their starting quarterback.

Dalton made three Pro Bowls with Cincinnati and helped lead the Bengals to five consecutive playoff appearances from 2011 through 2015.

Across 180 regular-season appearances with the Bengals, Cowboys, Bears, Saints, Panthers and Eagles, Dalton has compiled 39,793 passing yards, 254 touchdown passes and 152 interceptions, with an 87.4 career passer rating.

His career also includes 169 starts, with most coming during his nine-year tenure in Cincinnati.

Dalton turns 39 on October 29. If his release from Philadelphia is finalized, he will become an experienced free-agent option for teams seeking quarterback depth during the 2026 season.

title: Early season runs grind to a halt as Lyon loses at Lens and Dortmund held by Bremen
description: Lens ended Lyon’s unbeaten start to Ligue 1 while Borussia Dortmund dropped Bundesliga points for the first time this season after Werder Bremen rescue a late dramatic 2-2 draw on Friday.In Spain, Malaga was still without a win after drawing with visiting Espanyol 1-1.
fullText:
Lens ended Lyon's unbeaten start to Ligue 1 while Borussia Dortmund dropped Bundesliga points for the first time this season after Werder Bremen rescue a late dramatic 2-2 draw on Friday.

In Spain, Malaga was still without a win after drawing with visiting Espanyol 1-1.

Dortmund came into Friday's home match on top of the Bundesliga and the only club to win all four of its games so far.

While losing Amos Pieper to injury in the first half, Dortmund struggled to find a way past Karl Hein, who was outstanding in the Bremen goal. But even he could not hold stop Dortmund forever and the home side eventually seized control with goals in the 80th and 85th minutes from Daniel Svensson and Nico Schlotterbeck.

However, Bremen scored twice in the dying minutes to rescue an unlikely point.

Ludovit Reis cut the deficit with a low drive two minutes from time and former Dortmund forward Niclas Füllkrug shocked his old side with a headed equalizer in the second minute of stoppage time.

Matthieu Udol scored and was sent off as Lens put the brakes on Lyon's early season run in an unexpected 2-1 win.

Journeyman striker Florian Sotoca chested down a pass inside the box before swivelling and volleying home the opener for Lens 10 minutes before halftime. Udol made it 2-0 13 minutes from time with a header.

It was the second goal in two games for Udol but his joy turned to disappointment seven minutes later when he was shown a straight red card for a bad foul.

Lyon got a goal back almost immediately through Khalis Merah but Lens held on to give new coach Yannick Cahuzac his first win.

The result lifted Lens into seventh place. Lyon was second, two points behind leader Monaco.

Malaga's poor start in La Liga continued in a 1-1 draw with Espanyol.

It could have been a lot worse for the home side, which was behind for almost the entire game.

Bryan Zaragoza put visiting Espanyol ahead after 13 minutes when he cut in from the left, beat two men and drilled in a low shot.

But substitute Adrian Nino's volley in stoppage time gave Malaga its fourth point of the season. It remains the only club without a win and after eight games it is joint bottom of La Liga with Valencia.

Espanyol, meanwhile, climbed to 11th.

title: Romulus football cancels game due to threat to 'incite violence'
description: Romulus football canceled its homecoming game because the district received a "credible" threat of potential violence, according to a statement.
fullText:
Romulus football has cancelled its Week 7 homecoming game against Dearborn Heights Annapolis on Friday, Oct. 9, because the school district received "credible information that there is a coordinated intention to incite violence at tonight's game," according to an announcement from superintendent Benjamin Edmondson.

Edmonson said that students reported the threat to officials, allowing them "to inform the appropriate authorities in a timely manner."

"It is my responsibility as the superintendent to ensure the safety of our community and act with certainty particularly when receiving any threat of violence at our events," Edmonson said in the statement.

MORE PREPS: Michigan high school football live scores and updates for Week 7 games

The district did not indicate if the game against Annapolis would be made up on a different date. Romulus currently sits at 3-3 and in the middle of the pack in the Western Wayne Athletic Conference.

The district said it will be "transparent" and reveal more about the situation as they receive information. In the statement, Edmonson also urged parents to speak with their kids about reporting potentially concerning behavior.

"Today, we are able to avert a catastrophic event, but it takes just one moment of poor decision-making or failing to report a known threat that can permanently change the lives of one or many. Violence, of any sort, is not a manner in which to settle disputes and differences," Edmonson said in the statement.

title: NASCAR Cup Series Veteran Sounds Alarm Over O’Reilly Series’ Troubling Future
description: Denny Hamlin has raised concerns about the financial stability of the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, warning that losing one major team could weaken the competition across the field.The 23XI Racing co-owner discussed the issue on his Actions Detrimental podcast, where he talked about Sheldon Creed’s move from Haas Factory Team to Sam Hunt Racing.Hamlin welcomed […] The post NASCAR Cup Series Veteran Sounds Alarm Over O’Reilly Series’ Troubling Future appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Denny Hamlin has raised concerns about the financial stability of the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, warning that losing one major team could weaken the competition across the field.

The 23XI Racing co-owner discussed the issue on his Actions Detrimental podcast, where he talked about Sheldon Creed's move from Haas Factory Team to Sam Hunt Racing.

Hamlin welcomed the move as a positive step for Sam Hunt Racing but used it to explain the financial pressure facing teams in NASCAR's second-tier series.

He believes a small group of well-funded organizations provides much of the competitive equipment fans see each Saturday. If one of those teams withdraws, Hamlin warned, the series could struggle to maintain its current level of competition.

Hamlin praised Sam Hunt Racing for securing Creed, the current points leader, and described him as an experienced driver who could help the team compete.

"I think it's good for Sam Hunt. He gets a proven race winner. Sheldon Creed is a steady, very good driver. I think that's what that team needs too."

However, Hamlin also highlighted the challenges facing smaller NASCAR O'Reilly Series teams. Hamlin credited Sam Hunt Racing, Ryan Sieg, JR Motorsports and Joe Gibbs Racing for keeping the O'Reilly Series competitive, warning that losing any one of them could seriously weaken the field.

"And listen, God bless Sam Hunt, Ryan Sieg, Dale Jr., and Joe Gibbs because if any one of those dominoes fall, and that series looks like ARCA," Hamlin said.

He also mentioned Tommy Joe Martins' team and welcomed what he described as a positive move to Ford. Hamlin said he appreciated the work the organization puts into its equipment each week.

Hamlin said the financial challenges behind NASCAR O'Reilly Series competition help explain why drivers frequently move between teams.

Hamlin also highlighted JR Motorsports' importance to the series, warning that losing its five cars could leave a major gap in the competitive field.

"Yeah, I just, I'm telling you that series in my mind, it's just really fragile," Hamlin said. "Like if Dale Jr., for some reason, he's not going to, but like, could you imagine those five cars not on the grid? It's just, it's not good."

According to Hamlin, many drivers in the Saturday races pay team owners for their seats. This arrangement often forces drivers to compare financial offers rather than remain with organizations where they have established themselves.

"They're switching teams like musical chairs every year. And the unfortunate truth is that 80% of those drivers in the Saturday races are paying some sum of money to the team owner to drive those cars," Hamlin said.

He explained that team owners weigh competing offers, while drivers sometimes move elsewhere when they cannot meet the required financial terms.

Financial demands often push NASCAR O'Reilly Series drivers to switch teams, even when they have proven they can compete and win races.

Hamlin acknowledged that fans see a competitive product when they watch NASCAR O'Reilly Series races. However, he argued that the quality of the racing does not reflect the financial security of the organizations involved.

"I know it looks like the O'Reilly Series, from the fans' perspective, is the most solid series that NASCAR has, but I'm telling you it is the most fragile when it comes to finances," Hamlin said.

Hamlin believes top teams should prioritize proven drivers based on their ability to win races rather than how much money they bring to the organization. Instead, he argued, financial contributions from drivers play a major role in determining who gets those opportunities.

"Yeah, listen. The top 10 drivers in O'Reilly should be there because the owners just want them to go win races, but that is not the model that the O'Reilly Series is right now. I mean, that's just not the truth."

Hamlin's comments highlight the challenge facing NASCAR O'Reilly Series teams as they balance competitive equipment, sponsorship funding, and driver payments. While the series continues to deliver close racing, he warned that its financial foundation remains vulnerable if one of its leading organizations steps away.

title: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns to practice and is questionable for game with Packers
description: (AP) — Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returned to practice on a limited basis Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game at Green Bay.Williams has missed the Bears’ last two games since injuring his right hamstring during a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sept.
fullText:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. (AP) — Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returned to practice on a limited basis Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Green Bay.

Williams has missed the Bears' last two games since injuring his right hamstring during a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20. Bears coach Ben Johnson had indicated Monday that Williams wouldn't be available this weekend, but that was before the quarterback returned to practice.

"He's doing a great job with his rehab," Johnson said Monday. "He's not going to be there this week for us. We think it's still a week-to-week deal for us."

The Bears (3-1) have won each of the two games Williams has missed, with Case Keenum taking his place in a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles and Tyson Bagent starting in a 23-12 triumph over the New York Jets. Bagent is expected to start Sunday against the Packers (2-2) if Williams is unavailable.

In other injury news, the Bears ruled running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quadricep) for Sunday's game. Defensive back Kyler Gordon (calf), linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles), defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee) and Williams are questionable.

The Packers have ruled out running back Chris Brooks and wide receiver Savion Williams due to ankle injuries. Guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep) are doubtful. Center/guard Jager Burton (back) and defensive tackles Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Javon Hargrave (toe) are questionable.

title: Ex-Saints QB Suddenly Released by Eagles
description: In a successful and well-traveled NFL career, Andy Dalton had a stop with the New Orleans Saints. It wasn’t the most memorable or the longest, but it was substantial time on the field for “The Red Rifle” with the Saints. It came to mind again on Friday, when the Philadelphia Eagles surprisingly released Dalton after […] The post Ex-Saints QB Suddenly Released by Eagles appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
In a successful and well-traveled NFL career, Andy Dalton had a stop with the New Orleans Saints.

It wasn't the most memorable or the longest, but it was substantial time on the field for "The Red Rifle" with the Saints.

It came to mind again on Friday, when the Philadelphia Eagles surprisingly released Dalton after he'd spent a portion of this season as one of the backup QBs to Jalen Hurts.

Dalton's release wasn't necessarily expected, but the Eagles did have a surplus of quarterbacks and evidently felt one of those roster spots could be used elsewhere.

The veteran Dalton wasn't in the mix to start if Hurts remained healthy, and the Eagles went with a different look for their depth chart.

Tanner McKee, the tall right-handed passer, will be Hurts' main backup. He has gotten limited starting experience in the NFL and is believed by some to be an eventual trade candidate, given that he's well thought of around the league.

The Eagles' QB3 will be Cole Payton, the athletic lefty rookie from North Dakota State. Payton is more of a project, but he's got the right traits to succeed.

Dalton played for the Saints in the 2022 NFL season.

That was after he began his career with nine years with the Cincinnati Bengals, for whom he started 133 games.

Dalton went from Cincy to the Dallas Cowboys, and he made nine starts there in 2020.

Then in 2021, Dalton went to the Chicago Bears and got six starts.

The Saints were Dalton's team in 2022, and it was his last full season of his career. He started 14 games and went 6-8. Dalton completed 66.7% of his passes for 2,871 yards with 18 touchdowns and nine interceptions.

New Orleans also had Jameis Winston start three games that season, but it was Dalton who got the lion's share of the work — along with the occasional pass by Taysom Hill.

The Saints did win a memorable 39-32 game that season over the Seattle Seahawks, in which Dalton threw one touchdown to Chris Olave. But that game was really about Hill, who completed one pass for a 22-yard touchdown to Adam Trautman and then ran nine times for 112 yards and three more TDs, including a 60-yard score.

Dalton left the Saints after that year and went to the NFC South rival Carolina Panthers, and he started seven games there over three seasons.

He joined the Eagles for the 2026 season. Dalton will turn 39 on Oct. 29, and it's not clear how much longer he may have left in the NFL.

title: Latter-day Saint shortstop celebrates Brewers win with Fanta
description: Copper Pratt, who doesn't drink alcohol, sipped orange soda to celebrate Milwaukee's NLDS-clinching win over the San Diego Padres.
fullText:
Cooper Pratt's clubhouse celebration after the Milwaukee Brewers dispatched the San Diego Padres in the National League Division Series on Wednesday took on a little different flavor than the rest of the team's.

While some kind of alcohol is typically on ice for series-clinching wins or championships, the Brewers had soda ready for their locker room party.

Because Pratt, a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, doesn't drink alcohol, his teammates made sure there were bottles of Fanta Orange on hand for the rookie shortstop. The church admonishes members to abstain from alcohol.

"That Fanta tastes fantastic, man. That Fanta tastes fantastic. Tastes special, tastes special after that one, man," he exclaimed with goggles perched on his forehead.

Don't think it gets better than #Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt celebrating with soda.

"They didn't have sparkling cider, so I got some Fanta... tastes special after that one, frick!"@lanceallan | @CBS58 pic.twitter.com/Nnw8UWTkq0

The 21-year-old Pratt made his major league debut with the Brewers on June 16, 2026, after signing an eight-year, $50 million contract with the team. The Hialeah, Florida, native has held the starting shortstop job since.

Pratt missed Milwaukee's NL Central Division-clinching party in September at a hotel in Pittsburgh due to a contagious flu-like illness. He was isolated in a room and listened to the game on the radio before later receiving a T-shirt and sparkling cider.

"When I was sick, I was like, frick, we're going to win anyway. I'm going to be in my room. We're going to celebrate another time, another couple of times," he said.

Pratt hit .281 with 3 home runs and 34 RBI in 74 regular-season games. He's hitting .267 through four playoff games but has yet to drive in a run. Pratt's uncle, Trent Pratt, is the head baseball coach at BYU.

The Brewers, winners of a club-record 103 regular-season games, beat the Padres in San Diego to take the best-of-five division series in four games.

"Man, once we got the final out, I was pretty pumped up, man. Hearing the crowd go silent, just hearing the guys," Pratt told Fox6 News Milwaukee between swigs of orange soda. "It was special, especially on the road, getting to be the villain."

Milwaukee now faces the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, the team that bumped them from the playoffs last year. Pratt was injured when the Brewers played the Dodgers during the season.

"This will be the first time I've seen the Dodgers, just another game, same game. We're going to play the same. We're going to play to win," he said.

And if they do, the Brewers, no doubt, will have Fanta Orange in the cooler for the celebration.

title: Davis Webb calls demotion 'disappointing' after Sean Payton reclaims Broncos call sheet
description: (AP) — Davis Webb is leaning on his background as a backup quarterback to help him deal with his demotion as the Denver Broncos' offensive play-caller.Webb said he's disappointed Sean Payton stripped him of his play-calling duties after just four games but he's eager to see how the offense responds when the Broncos visit the Los Angeles Chargers this weekend.
fullText:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. (AP) — Davis Webb is leaning on his background as a backup quarterback to help him deal with his demotion as the Denver Broncos' offensive play-caller.

Webb said he's disappointed Sean Payton stripped him of his play-calling duties after just four games but he's eager to see how the offense responds when the Broncos visit the Los Angeles Chargers this weekend.

"Long week in some ways but in other ways, back to work," Webb said Friday in his first public comments since Payton took back play-calling duties from his new offensive coordinator in a bid to jolt the Broncos' sputtering offense.

"I'm still in charge of running the offensive meetings and helping out the quarterback room and that's where we're at," Webb said.

Payton met with Webb on Monday and told him he was taking back the call sheet and would be the one in quarterback Bo Nix's ear once again.

Webb said the talk lasted about an hour but he declined to say whether he fought to keep his play-calling duties: "That was a private conversation; we'll keep it as such. But it was an hour long and he made a decision and that's his job. He's the head coach of the football team and my job now is to do this role even better."

The talk "probably wasn't easy for him," said Webb, who said it was a difficult discussion for himself: "Yeah, I think anytime that happens in any aspect of your life job-wise, it is, a little bit. But in the same breath, that's the NFL. You get going. I've been a backup QB, I've been up and down before. And that's kind of how it goes."

Webb's four-game tryout came against teams with a combined 13-3 record.

The Broncos' two wins were against the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) and the preseason NFC Super Bowl-favorite Los Angeles Rams (2-2) and their two losses were on the road to two of the league's last three remaining unbeaten teams in Kansas City and San Francisco, both 4-0.

So, was four tough games enough of an audition? Webb was asked.

"Luckily, that's not my job" to decide, Webb said. "That's his job. But obviously, I think he answered that."

Asked what lessons he took, Webb said, "I think it was a smaller sample size than maybe you would like for a full season, but within the four weeks every week the operation was cleaner."

Although Webb was quicker in getting calls into his quarterback than Payton was last season, allowing Nix more time at the line of scrimmage to survey the field and decipher the defense, that failed to translate into faster starts.

The Broncos have managed just 13 first-half points so far. Nix hasn't been playing well, the offense has committed a slew of penalties and the run-pass balance has been out of whack.

Payton insisted that despite this demotion, Webb, who went straight from being a backup QB for the New York Giants to serving as Nix's position coach in 2023, is still on the fast track to becoming an NFL head coach.

Webb had some opportunities to leave Denver in this most recent coaching cycle but he stayed after Payton offered to let him call plays. That opportunity, Webb said last summer, made staying "a no-brainer."

Given Denver's Super Bowl aspirations, Payton's long resume as one of football's top play-callers and the tough early schedule, Webb said he knew something like this could happen to him this season.

"I've taught myself early to think about the best- and worst-case scenarios," Webb said, "and if you're OK with both, then take that job on."

Notes: The Broncos re-signed WR Lil'Jordan Humphrey to their practice squad and added CB Ugochukwu Amadi to their practice squad Friday.

title: Simsbury basketball standout Declan Griffiths, CT's top-ranked recruit, commits to Vanderbilt
description: Declan's father, Larry, played Division I basketball at Hartford, while his brother, Gavin, is returning to Temple for his senior season.
fullText:
Four-star prospect and St. Thomas More star Declan Griffiths committed to Vanderbilt on Friday afternoon, according to On3.

The 6-foot-7 wing, whom Rivals ranks No. 1 in Connecticut and No. 35 nationally, projects as a high-level frontcourt shooting threat, taking nearly 80% of his shots from 3-point range. Griffiths chose the SEC program over interest from Ole Miss, Butler and regional programs Boston College and Providence.

Griffiths hails from Simsbury and began his high school career at neighboring Avon Old Farms, where the Beavers went 10-13 last season. He participated in the Ta'Quan Zimmerman Elite 20 Invitational at Shelton High School over the summer, an event that also featured five-star UConn target Malachi Jordan, and will continue his high school career at St. Thomas 

"I'm looking for a good fit," Griffiths told CTInsider last month, "a system I can succeed in that's had players like me do very well - shooters, spacers, athletic wings."

Griffiths's brother, Gavin, also emerged as a prized wing shooter, blossoming into a borderline five-star prospect at the Kingswood-Oxford School and even landing on Dan Hurley's radar at UConn. Ultimately, Gavin committed to Rutgers as the highest-ranked recruit of coach Steve Pikiell's tenure. He struggled to meet those lofty expectations in New Jersey, shooting 33% from the field in two seasons at Rutgers and Nebraska before finding more success at Temple last season.

Larry Griffiths, the father of the two recruits, was himself a two-time All-State center at Cheshire. He starred at the nearby University of Hartford, where he scored 1,181 points, ranks third in program history with 694 rebounds and was inducted into its Alumni Athletics Hall of Fame in 2004.

title: Yankees Fans Demand Aaron Boone Firing
description: After a 3-0 ALDS sweep by the Rays, a massive poll shows Yankees fans want Aaron Boone and Brian Cashman gone. The Bronx is boiling over.
fullText:
Most people expect fans to be upset after a playoff sweep. They don't expect them to call for a total purge of the leadership. According to a recent The Post poll, over 11,000 voters indicate that nearly 85 percent desire Aaron Boone's removal from the dugout. The numbers are staggering. The Bronx is not just angry; it is looking for an exit strategy for the entire management team.

The fallout follows a brutal three-game sweep at the hands of the Tampa Bay Rays. New York lost every game in the American League Division Series. The season ended on Wednesday night with a 4-3 loss at Yankee Stadium. It was the final blow in a series where the Yankees could not find a way to win. Now, the fans are turning their sights on the front office and the dugout.

The frustration extends far beyond the manager. According to Yahoo Sports, 73 percent of those who voted in the poll—totaling 8,535 people—want Brian Cashman to lose his job. Cashman has held his position as general manager for 29 seasons. While he has seen four World Series titles and seven pennants, the recent lack of success is wearing thin. One voter even suggested that "Cashman should go or change the organization's approach to hitting."

The roster construction is a major pain point for the fanbase.

The physical toll of the series was visible on the field. Aaron Boone described a "broken clubhouse" after the Wednesday night loss. The team struggled to produce at the plate, and the lineup changes did not help. For instance, Trent Grisham went 0-for-11 during the ALDS. The manager also benched Jazz Chisholm Jr. for the start of Game 3. Chisholm Jr. had very little to say about the decision, telling reporters, "No comment. Next."

While some players are facing criticism, others are seeing their value rise. Anthony Volpe appeared to be a bright spot despite the team's failure. About 79 percent of poll participants believe he should stay with the franchise. This stands in stark contrast to the sentiment regarding veteran sluggers. Per Yahoo Sports, 86 percent of voters want Giancarlo Stanton gone, and 91 percent want Jazz Chisholm Jr. off the roster.

The lack of recent glory is hard to ignore. The Yankees have not won a World Series since 2009. This 17-year drought is a heavy weight on the franchise. Even MLB legend Alex Rodriguez noted that "something has to change" following the Game 3 loss. The fans are no longer willing to wait for a turnaround that never seems to arrive.

Some fans are even threatening to walk away entirely. A Barstool Sports personality, Tommy Smokes, claimed he is boycotting the team until serious changes occur. He wrote on X that he is done caring about the franchise because it is a "loser, complacent franchise." The tension in New York is at an all-time high, and the offseason promises to be a period of massive upheaval.

title: Page boys capture TSSAA golf state championship; Poppy Pewitt repeats in AA girls
description: The 2026 TSSAA golf state tournament ended with Class AA and Division II-AA competition, including a first team title and multiple repeat champions.
fullText:
SEVIERVILLE ― The 2026 TSSAA golf season concluded by crowning the winners of Class AA and Division II-AA boys and girls competition at Sevierville Golf Course on Oct. 9.

Page boys brought fireworks as a pair of Patriots teammates settled the individual Class AA state championship in two playoff holes while the team cruised to the AA title. Page's girls finished state runners-up behind Ooltewah.

Memphis University School claimed captured the Division II-AA boys crown, and Baylor held off Harpeth Hall to win in DII-AA girls.

TSSAA GOLF: FRA's Walker Webb repeats as TSSAA golf state champ; CAK, Summertown claim team titles

Senior Jack Eickhoff and junior Reid Bostelman made sure Page would claim the program's first TSSAA golf championship by finishing in a tie atop the leaderboard after 18 holes on Oct. 9, shooting 139s.

But it was Eickhoff who captured the individual state title, beating Bostelman in a playoff. Eickhoff birdied the second playoff hole to claim the title. Eickhoff, who led after the first day with a 68, finished 5-under par (139). Bostelman mounted a furious comeback on the second day, shooting 6-under, 66, the lowest round in the two days of Class AA competition.

Page lapped the field with a final score of 11-under (565). It finished 41 strokes ahead of Houston in second place while Science Hill finished third (611).

It's the first team state championship for the Patriots who finished runner-up in 2022. Carson Jenkins finished tied for fifth (142) while Brayden Bennett tied for 12th (145).

A pair of elite golfers from the Memphis area drove their team to the overall victory in DII-AA. Seniors Brantley Moore and Drew Knighton secured the top two spots to lead MUS to the program's eighth overall TSSAA championship. The Owls ended seven strokes ahead of Ensworth an 11-under (565).

Moore repeated as the state champion with the lowest overall score in the tournament across all classes. He notched 68 on both days to end with an 8-under (136), one stroke better than Franklin Road Academy's Walker Webb, who captured the DII-A state crown on Oct. 6.

Knighton tied with Christian Brothers' Patrick Gatti for second place. Both matched each other with a 70 on both days of competition and finished 4-under (140).

MUS also had senior Charles Snider tie for fourth, sophomore Jack Faber tie in 20th and sophomore Harris Laughlin tie for 25th to round out their state title team.

In 2025, Dickson County's Poppy Pewitt won the Class AA girls state title with an even par (140). A year later, the junior and individual competitor improved that score by a single stroke.

Pewitt shot a 1-under, 139, to repeat as the state champion and finished two strokes ahead of Ooltewah's Alli Troxell. Troxell helped Ooltewah defeat Page in Class AA with a team score of 12-over (292).

Hardin Valley took third as a team with a 312.
